chunks: And among its most wonderful [words] is his (peace be upon him) saying:
Behold, today is the day of preparation (the racecourse), and tomorrow is the day of the race; the starting point is Paradise and the destination is Hell,

for within it—besides the sublimity of the wording, the greatness of the meaning, the truthfulness of the simile, and the factual nature of the illustration—lies a wonderful secret and a delicate implication,

key_terms.السَّبَقَةُ: The starting point or the initial grant; referring to Paradise as the beginning of the journey.
key_terms.السِّبَاقَ: The race or competition; the actual event of the afterlife or the final reckoning.
key_terms.الْغَايَةَ: The destination or end point; referring to Hell as the final outcome for the unsuccessful.
key_terms.الْمِضْمَارَ: The racecourse or place of preparation; the current worldly life where one prepares for the afterlife.
key_terms.صَادِقِ التَّمْثِيلِ: The truthful or accurate nature of the simile/metaphor used.
key_terms.فَخَامَةِ اللَّفْظِ: The sublimity and nobility of the wording/style.

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of 'today is the racecourse and tomorrow is the race' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the vivid metaphor of a racecourse (midmar) to illustrate that worldly life is merely a preparatory stage for the ultimate contest of the Hereafter. This narration, celebrated in Shia scholarship for its rhetorical precision, underscores the urgency of spiritual striving, framing Paradise as the initial reward of grace and Hell as the final consequence of failure. The text invites reflection on the transient nature of time as a divine opportunity for self-purification before the final reckoning.

en.sayed-ali-raza: His most wonderful words in this sermon are “
Today is the day of preparation while tomorrow is the day of race. The place to proceed to is Paradise while the place of doom is Hell,”
because besides sublimity of words, greatness of meaning, true similes and factual illustrations, there are wonderful secrets and delicate implications therein.
